projects.name: Water Main Replacement
projects.desc: This project consists of replacing approximately 10,050 linear feet of old, deteriorating, and undersized cast iron pipe and undersized PVC pipes. Parker currently experiences water and pressure loss due to old pipes. There is a potential for drinking water contamination due to a petroleum contamination plume identified in the area. The existing 2 inch cast iron pipes are too small for the current flow and pressure demands. If there is a fire on the south side of Business Highway 98, fire hoses must be pulled from the north side causing a dangerous traffic and firefighting situation. This project will help reduce water loss by replacing the deteriorating pipes. Upsizing some of the mains will improve water pressure, both for residential use and for firefighting. The risk of contamination will be greatly reduced as PVC does not corrode internally or become contaminated like cast iron. There will be adequate and easy fire protection for the south side of the affected area.

projects.name: Cheri Lane Stormwater Improvements
projects.desc: This project consists of acquisition of Parker's primary flood-prone area and construction of a stormwater retention pond and treatment facilities, including culverts, drainage pipes and ditches. This project dovetails with the recently completed project just north of this site that provides the first stage of retention and treatment. Buildings in the flood area are deteriorated and likely unsafe due to past and frequent flooding. Another level of stormwater treatment is needed to protect the surrounding waterbodies. This project will provide a second stage of stormwater retention and treatment prior to the stormwater entering Pitts Bayou and St. Andrews Bay. It will better alleviate stormwater runoff in surrounding neighborhoods and alleviate continued unsafe living conditions in the structures on the flood site.

projects.name: Water Main Replacement
projects.desc: This project consists of replacing approximately 23,450 linear feet of old, deteriorating, and undersized cast iron pipe and undersized PVC pipes on the west side of Business Highway 98, adding new 8 inch PVC main to the east side, and installing fire hydrants on the east side and for areas on the west side that do not have adequate fire protection. Parker currently experiences water and pressure loss due to old pipes. The existing 2 inch cast iron pipes are too small for the current flow and pressure demands, and the lack of main water lines on the east side restrict fire protection and economic development. If there is a fire on the east side of Business Highway 98, fire hoses must be pulled from the west side causing a dangerous traffic and firefighting situation. Upsizing some of the mains will improve water pressure, both for residential use and for firefighting. There will be adequate and easy fire protection for the east side of the affected area and new service can be provided to residential and business customers.

projects.name: Bay Parkway (Loop Road Phase 2)
projects.desc: This project is the connection of Bay Parkway Phase 1 eastward down the power line easement and ties into Nautilus St. This will be a public roadway with associated connector road crossing to help facilitate movement from east to west. Traffic congestion exists year round. All surrounding Florida Department of Transportation roadways are over capacity and the level of service does not accommodate the current flow of traffic. Traffic in this area is projected to increase in coming years further increasing congestion. This road will provide an alternative limited access route to bypass around Pier Park, Frank Brown Park, and the Palmetto Trace subdivision once the connector road is complete. This alternate roadway will alleviate existing and future traffic congestion. The Project is estimated to redirect 14% of the volume from the Panama City Beach Parkway and State Road 79 intersection.

projects.name: County Road 2300 Repaving

With substantial pavement deterioration along this stretch, improving this connection and upgrading the pavement to account for the expected increase in traffic is essential.
